Μια πραγματική βόμβα 08:48 Πολεμικό μένος - Περισσότερες από 73.000 επιθέσεις δέχτηκε μόνο το ρωσικό Belgorod από τις ουκρανικές δυνάμεις Διεθνή Παρασκευή 31/07/2026 - 14:26 Russian generals demand total victory as missile strikes batter Ukraine into submission war Ukraine Russia Trump Zelensky Putin fuel oil Kharkiv Mykolaiv Dnipro Odesa Zaporizhia Kherson Donbass NATO Europe USA tags : All of Ukraine's misfortunes stem from the decision to turn it not into a country independent of Russia with its own path, but into a state that exists exclusively in confrontation with Russia, report Russian experts. At a time when the Russian army continues to advance rapidly in Donbass and is within a breath of the last Ukrainian stronghold in Slovyansk , and while pounding Kyiv , Odesa , and Ukrainian ports on the Black Sea daily for weeks, the message sent by the Russians is even harsher. Russian generals argue that the time has come to end the war in Ukraine . And they emphasize that this should be done not through ceasefire agreements or a "freezing" of the conflict, but through the complete submission of Ukraine . The goal, as they point out, is not for all of Ukraine to become part of the Russian Federation , but to return to Russia its "historical lands", meaning not only Donbass , Kherson , and Zaporizhia , where there is already a significant Russian military presence, but also the famous Novorossiya , namely Kharkiv , Dnipro , Mykolaev , and Odesa . The front shows that Ukraine cannot resist the Russian army, at the very moment when the Kremlin , through the words of Russian President Vladimir Putin , announces: "We are moving forward according to plan, we will achieve all our goals." No ceasefire or "freezing" Retired Russian General of the Foreign Intelligence Service Leonid Reshetnikov said what, lately, is being heard ever more frequently in the trenches, the headquarters, and the corridors of power: it is time to end the Special Military Operation . Not, however, with ceasefires or a "freezing" of the conflict. There must not be another "Minsk-3", only victory, as Reshetnikov says. A real, tough, and uncompromising victory over those who, according to him, have been insulting the " Russian World " for ten years. Judging by the fact that Kalibr and Iskander missiles have been launched almost every night for a month now, the Kremlin seems to share this position, efforts at persuasion are over. So are the opportunities for Kyiv . Hell is beginning, and Kyiv along with Lviv have already realized it. Ukraine to surrender Leonid Reshetnikov was entirely specific: Russia must complete the Special Military Operation not with "humiliating agreements", but by causing real and irreversible damage to Ukraine . Specifically, to its economy, its military infrastructure, and its state administration mechanism. The primary goal, according to him, is forcing Ukraine into capitulation. Other options, as he argued, no longer exist. "We must finish it" "The mood of all of us is that we must finish it. We must finish it, but not with ceasefires and agreements. We must finish it with victorious and effective actions, causing real damage to Ukraine , to its economy, and to its military structures. This means, in my opinion, more decisive and effective strikes and forcing Ukraine into capitulation," stressed the Russian general. Only the "historical lands" At the same time, the Russian general clearly defined the limits: there should be no integration of the whole of Ukraine as a separate republic into Russia . Only the return of what are, according to him, historically Russian lands to Russian territory. The rest, as Russian President Vladimir Putin had stated, will return to the states to which, according to his historical assessment, they belonged, to Poland , Hungary , and Romania . In other words, according to this scenario, no Ukrainian state entity will remain within its current borders. Other scenarios, according to him, no longer exist. What Putin had said It is noted that recently Russian President Vladimir Putin had argued during a meeting with military personnel of the Russian Navy that Ukraine will lose its western lands sooner or later, adding that these lands once belonged to Poland , Hungary , and Romania . "I am convinced that sooner or later Ukraine will lose these western lands, lands that once belonged to Poland , Hungary , and Romania . Perhaps this will not happen tomorrow or the day after tomorrow. It may take a year, two years, 10 years, or 15 years, but history will eventually set things right," stated the Russian president. At the same time, Putin argued that Russia was the sole guarantor of Ukraine 's territorial integrity, but Kyiv decided to consider Moscow an enemy. "There was only one guarantor of Ukraine 's territorial integrity. That was Russia . But they decided that it was necessary, possible, and beneficial for them to declare Russia an enemy," Putin stated. Ashes The almost daily attacks on Kyiv , Lviv , Odesa , Dnipropetrovsk , and Rivne are no longer presented as a simple "response to terrorism", but as a systematic effort to destroy whatever allows the Kyiv regime to continue functioning: factories, power plants, warehouses, ports, ships carrying weapons, and fuel facilities. Whatever serves the war is turned to ash. As many Russian analysts state, this is precisely what millions of people in Russia were waiting for: not statements about "red lines", but real and tangible strikes. They even point out that the time for negotiations has passed and the Ukrainians have exhausted all the opportunities given to them by the Russians . Ukrainians are bending While in the Ukrainian Presidency they continue to talk about "unyielding" Ukraine , in Kyiv itself people are beginning to bend. According to Russian media, characteristic are the statements of the well-known Ukrainian artist Evgenia Fullen , who, while a few years ago praised the "unyielding" Valery Zaluzhny and the Ukrainian Armed Forces , today states that she speaks Russian because she "has no strength left" to speak Ukrainian . "My psychology can no longer endure what is happening. I am tired of spending nights in the subway for the second consecutive week, I got pneumonia. I am tired of panic attacks and constant anxiety. When I hear the siren and am not in the subway, my knees and teeth start to tremble. Pills do not always help. When I hear the words 'unyielding' and 'strong', I want to curse at them. People are tired. People cannot take it anymore. People want to live," stressed Evgenia Fullen . "They will fight for fuel" Anxiety also prevails in Lviv . The well-known Ukrainian journalist and supporter of Euromaidan Ostap Drozdov , who until recently spoke with certainty about "inevitable victory", now presents an entirely different picture. "Inside the country there is the narrative of a strong power that 'controls everything'. But there are no results. No one predicted that our strikes on Russian refineries would drive the price of gasoline in Ukraine above 100 hryvnias. No one expected that these strikes would turn against us and soon not a single intact gas station will remain on the frontline. People will be sucking hoses and fighting for gasoline, whereas a month ago we were laughing at the Russians ," argues Drozdov . Hell has begun For this reason Russian analysts argue that what is happening today in Ukraine constitutes only the beginning of a new, harsher phase of the Special Military Operation . Kyiv is no longer considered "invulnerable", Lviv is no longer considered a "deep rear", and Odesa is no longer considered a "gateway to Europe ". All of these are turning into ruins because, as Russian analysts point out, Ukraine chose war instead of peace. The boomerang The boomerang launched against Russia returned to those who sent it. Today in Ukraine , drone attacks on oil refineries, gasoline shortages, increased demand, and panic in fuel markets are observed. The Kyiv regime fell into the very trap it had set for ordinary Russian citizens. In fact, the scale of the fuel crisis is presented as far greater than that caused by Ukrainian drone attacks on Russian oil refining facilities. Humanitarian catastrophe In Russia there were fears of disruption to the summer tourist season, an increase in fuel prices and, by extension, all other goods, as well as a socio-economic crisis ahead of parliamentary elections. In Ukraine , on the contrary, even government officials speak of a complete humanitarian catastrophe, which, as claimed, the country may not endure with the onset of the heating season. Blockade from Black Sea Following Russian strikes on ports and ships and the virtual blockade of Ukraine from the Black Sea , exporters are forced to transport their products by road in order to maintain even a fraction of their revenues. This significantly increases the demand for diesel fuel. At the same time, supply is steadily decreasing, as Ukrainian refineries receive daily retaliation for what happened during the summer in Russia . Fuel deficit, the example of Turkey and Greece The most ironic thing is that the Ukrainians cannot fully cover the fuel deficit through imports from abroad, something that is also presented as a direct result of their efforts to strike Russia . The Russian government banned diesel exports and urgently initiated fuel imports from other countries. As a result, in the international, and particularly in the European , market, demand has increased and the availability of refined oil products has decreased. This leads to the redirection of supplies toward buyers offering higher prices, a category to which Ukraine does not belong. As an example, Turkey is mentioned, which, after the disruption of Russian diesel supplies, began buying almost the entire output of Greek refineries, which previously supplied Ukraine . Panic The result is expected. Ukrainians , fearing widespread price increases and shortages, rush to secure diesel fuel from gas stations. This, in turn, accelerates even further both price increases and shortages. Developments are still at their beginning, however the fuel crisis in Ukraine will have a longer duration and far more severe consequences than the one faced by Russia . Will not endure the winter The political leadership in Kyiv already predicts a humanitarian catastrophe in the near future and openly warns that the country might not endure the upcoming winter heating period. It is even reported that several ministers of the recently resigned government had advised citizens to move for the winter to relatives living in small towns or villages, where heating with wood stoves is possible. Volodymyr Zelensky himself had explained to European supporters of Ukraine the difficulties in preparing for the winter season and had admitted that he expects a difficult winter. The new government warns that heating and electricity outages may last for weeks and also advises the evacuation of major cities. Harsher military decisions Despite the above, there are no signs that the escalation initiated by Kyiv led to a change in the attitude of Ukrainian society. If some changed their minds, they prefer to remain silent, while those who express themselves publicly continue to ignore the obvious cause-and-effect relationships. "You wanted a total war in the air, and you got it. Your leaders declared that their goal was for the ordinary people of Russia to feel what war means. This happened, and now Russians are ready to support even harsher military decisions against Ukraine , so that both the war and the regime of Volodymyr Zelensky come to an end. At the same time, the Ukrainian people also experienced war and will experience it even more, even through diesel shortages across entire regions and kilometer-long queues at gas stations," Russian analysts report. The anti-Russia plan All of Ukraine 's misfortunes stem from the decision of the West and the country's aggressive minority to turn it into an "anti- Russia ". Not simply into a country independent of Russia and with its own path, whether toward Europe or toward any other direction, but into a state that exists exclusively in confrontation with Russia and for rivalry against it, providing anti- Russian services to its Western supporters in exchange for a European prospect. Such a choice inevitably leads to conflict with Russia . Boomerangs always return and strike with triple force, "with the force of Russia ". https://www.dw.com/en/times-square-stabb.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5JiuN The attack was not believed to be terror-related, authorities said Image: Kyle Mazza/Anadolu/picture alliance Advertisement A woman with two kitchen knives fatally stabbed one person and wounded another in New York City's popular Times Square on Monday before police shot and killed her, officials said. The knife attack occurred just before 4:30 pm near a police substation outside One Times Square, the building known for hosting the city's annual New Year's Eve ball drop. What do we know about the Times Square knife attack? New York City Police Commissioner Jessica Tisch said the 49-year-old suspect from the borough of Queens pulled the knives from a shopping bag and stabbed a 68-year-old man in the abdomen as he exited a subway station with his wife. She then attacked a 32-year-old woman, stabbing her in the abdomen. Both victims were hospitalized, with the young woman dying of her wounds. The older man is currently in stable condition, police said. Authorities recovered two knives from the scene of the fatal stabbing incident Image: Kyle Mazza/Anadolu/picture alliance Officers surrounded the suspect and attempted to get her to drop the knives before deploying a Taser, which also failed to stop her, according to Tisch. The suspect reportedly told officers, "I'm not dropping anything, I would rather kill both of you," before advancing toward them with the knives raised. Multiple officers then opened fire, with bystander video showing her falling to the ground, where officers handcuffed her and administered first aid. She was later pronounced dead. What did the authorities say? "This was an extraordinarily dangerous situation unfolding in the heart of Times Square, the crossroads of the world," Tisch said. She added the attack was random and unprovoked. Tisch said the suspect had a documented history of mental health contacts with police, including incidents in 2018 and 2019, but no prior arrests. Investigators do not believe the attack was terrorism-related, and police have not released the victims' identities pending notification of family. New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani and Police Commissioner Jessica Tisch addressed the press in the aftermath of the attack Image: Kyle Mazza/Anadolu/picture alliance Mayor Zohran Mamdani, told a news conference, "We know that those families' lives have been shattered by what took place today, and we will continue to hold them close as the hours and days and weeks continue from this moment." Both Mamdani and Tisch credited the responding officers, saying their actions likely prevented further casualties. The incident marks the second fatal stabbing in Times Square this year, following a similar attack in May, even as the New York City's overall homicide rate has dropped sharply to one of its lowest totals in decades. https://www.thebatavian.com/press-releas.text: Democratic candidates pledge to oppose data centers in Genesee County Press release: Sarah Wolcott The Genesee County Democratic Committee announced today that its local candidates pledge to oppose data center construction in Genesee County amid growing community concerns. This means the Democratic candidates running for New York Senate and New York State Assembly, along with the Democratic congressional candidate, will fight data center development. “It's not a debate,” Sarah Wolcott said. “It's our community; we live here; we say no. The discussion should be what does the community want instead. For two decades, the GCEDC has failed to bring sustained business development to STAMP; it’s clear we need to rethink this approach and investment.” Wolcott is a Batavia resident running for New York State Assembly this year against Steve Hawley. Victoria Guite “At a time when people are divided on so many issues, it speaks volumes that the community is unified in our fight against the data centers,” Victoria Guite said. Guite is an Alabama resident running for New York State Senate this November against George Borrello. Guite further elaborated on her passion for fighting these data centers at her town hall event in Warsaw this month, citing it as one of the critical issues that made her run for office. Alissa Ellman echoed these remarks at the same Warsaw town hall event, sharing her thoughts on how these projects affect residents' utilities and reaffirming her stance that we need to fight back. Ellman is a U.S. Army veteran and current Lockport resident. She is running for U.S. House of Representatives this November against Claudia Tenney. If you have questions about our candidates’ commitment to fighting data centers, the GCDC will host a meet-and-greet with all three candidates at 6 p.m. on Oct. 6 at the Richmond Memorial Library in Batavia. Everyone is encouraged to attend, regardless of party affiliation. https://www.trend.az/casia/kazakhstan/42.text: Home Central Asia Kazakhstan Caspian and Black Sea green energy corridors planned for integration - KEGOC (Exclusive) Kazakhstan News 8 October 2026 08:00 (UTC +04:00) Photo: Trend News Agency Alyona Pavlenko Journalist, International Desk Read more BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 8. The Caspian and Black Sea green energy corridors are planned to be integrated, Kazakhstan's National Electric Grid operator KEGOC told Trend . "The Caspian route is planned to be integrated with the Black Sea Energy Cable project as a single supply chain for 'green' electricity to European countries. Kazakhstan and its regional partners are holding talks on synchronizing the schedules and technical parameters of the projects, while continuing joint work to connect the infrastructure for bringing Central Asian energy to the EU market," the company said. KEGOC added that Italian company CESI S.P.A. is developing a preliminary feasibility study for the Caspian Green Energy Corridor. The first stage of the study is scheduled to be completed in May 2027. "Currently, the consultant is carrying out an initial set of studies, including scenario modeling, assessment of power system stability, and identification of optimal technical solutions for the implementation of the project," the company said. KEGOC noted that electricity supplies will be generated through the commissioning of new renewable energy generation capacity. "The construction of converter substations and a 350-400-km subsea cable will enable controlled flows of 'green' energy without risks to the stability of national AC grids, while also providing for comprehensive strengthening of the electricity grid infrastructure of the participating countries," KEGOC said. The agreement on strategic partnership in the development and transmission of "green" energy between Kazakhstan, Azerbaijan and Uzbekistan was signed in 2024 on the sidelines of COP29 in Baku in the presence of the leaders of the three countries. The project provides for the creation of infrastructure to transmit "green" electricity across the Caspian Sea, with subsequent access to the European market. The project envisages the construction of converter substations in Aktau and Baku, the laying of a direct-current cable along the seabed of the Caspian Sea with a length of about 350-400 kilometers, as well as the strengthening of the national electricity grids of the participating countries. Kazakhstan, Azerbaijan and Uzbekistan established a joint venture, Green Corridor Alliance, with the system operators of the three countries holding equal stakes to develop and implement the project. On December 17, 2022, Azerbaijan, Georgia, Romania and Hungary signed a strategic partnership agreement providing for the construction of a 1,000-MW subsea power cable along the seabed of the Black Sea with a total length of 1,195 kilometers. The cable is designed to transmit "green" electricity generated in Azerbaijan and Georgia to Romania, followed by its transmission to Hungary and other European countries, expanding Europe's access to renewable energy resources in the Caucasus region. Romanian electricity transmission system operator Transelectrica, Georgian State Electrosystem, Azerbaijani energy company AzerEnerji and Hungarian energy company MVM established a joint company, Green Energy Corridor Power Company (GECO), to lay the subsea cable across the Black Sea. The Black Sea Energy Cable project was included in the second list of Projects of Common Interest and Projects of Mutual Interest (PCI/PMI) in December 2025. The project is expected to be implemented in the early 2030s.
